notes: §1985:XV.2.1.3 GR2: without WITH DEBUGGING MODE "any USE FOR DEBUGGING statements and all associated debugging sections are compiled as if they were comment lines". The comment treatment is applied AFTER parsing: ProcedureTableBuilder.DeclCollectSection returns before binding a debugging section when DebuggingModeDeclared is false, and VersionConformancePass.VisitDeclarativeSection visits only the USE statement, so a well-formed body's semantics are ignored (probes: an undefined name, DEBUG-* references, an undefined procedure subject, GO TO a nondeclarative paragraph and a paragraph-name reused outside all compile, and no section runs; EXHIBIT NAMED and READY TRACE parse). But the section's text still has to parse: a body line that is not COBOL syntax is refused, though comment lines may hold any text. Witness: a well-formed section that must not run. kb/Work PB5291 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-67.json).

next.reason: 1985: "If the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is not specified in the SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph ... compiled as if they were comment lines"; 2023: "SOURCE-COMPUTER rules cover only computer-name-1 and the source computer; no WITH DEBUGGING MODE or USE FOR DEBUGGING". The 2023 SOURCE-COMPUTER rules no longer mention debugging mode, and no candidate has USE FOR DEBUGGING. The Debug module feature is absent from 2023.
